newsitem.title: CHINA: China to cut antimony output by 20 pct - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: China to cut antimony output by 20 pct - newspaper.

text.p: China will cut production of the metal antimony by 20 percent in the next few months to boost declining prices, the China Daily newspaper said on Friday.

China, which has about 50 percent of the world's known reserves of antimony, had seen domestic and international production rise but prices tumble over the last two years, the official newspaper said.
"As a result, the State wants to limit its production," it quoted the National Production Union for Antimony as saying.
It gave no details of total production. China releases total output figures for 10 nonferrous metals but does not give breakdowns.
Antimony is a silvery-white, brittle chemical element used to harden alloys.
Exports of unwrought antimony and antimony alloys soared to 15,244 tonnes in the first seven months of 1996, up 53.8 percent from a year ago.
Antimony prices were currently lower than production costs, forcing many makers to halt production, the China Daily said.
It said some firms had broken regulations by selling at low prices into a sluggish market, weakening buyer enthusiasm.
China had already closed many small antimony plants because of high pollution, reducing output levels, it said but gave no details of how Beijing would ensure further production cuts.
